items.label: Table 3, normal data, SD 40% of the control mean, equal arms (18 rows x 21 cells)

cause.summary: One cell of 378 is outside the tolerance: SMD 0.2, 100/100, k 5: % power, tau 0.5, RoM, 21 in the paper against 23.34 (tolerance 2.26). It is Monte Carlo error. Our second run, with other seeds, gives 22.29, within tolerance, and MD and SMD of the same row sit as far from the paper's 21 as RoM does: one draw of 10,000 meta-analyses moves all three. The table's RMS z is 0.97.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The cell is a chance miss of our run
hypotheses.test: The same design with another seed (second_run in comparison.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: A systematic difference in the power or the CI
hypotheses.test: Every other power and coverage cell of Tables 3-8 is within tolerance, and the table's RMS z is near 1

assumptions.what: Heterogeneity: each trial's experimental and control means are shifted independently, each by SD 0.5/sqrt(2) SD units, so that their difference has SD 0.5 (Methods)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper gives the SD per arm and the square-root sum that holds for independent shifts. One shift of SD 0.5 on the experimental mean only leaves 921 of 1080 tau = 0.5 cells of Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 within tolerance; one shared shift on both means (no heterogeneity left in the difference), 364; independent shifts, 1079.

assumptions.what: The study-specific shifts are normal; the paper does not name their distribution
assumptions.sensitivity: Not varied. Every tau = 0.5 cell comes back with normal shifts (1079 of 1080).

assumptions.what: % bias of RoM is 100 x (mean of the 10,000 back-transformed pooled RoMs - true RoM) / true RoM, the same definition as for MD and SMD. The paper says only 'a percentage of the true parameter value'
assumptions.sensitivity: On this scale 216 of 216 printed RoM bias cells of Tables 3-8 are within tolerance; on the ln RoM scale 97, and as a share of RoM - 1 65.

assumptions.what: I2 (%) is 100 x (1 - 1/m), with m the mean of Q/(k - 1) over the 10,000 replicates (the Table legends speak of 'the ratio of Q/(k-1)'). The paper does not say how I2 was summarized over replicates
assumptions.sensitivity: 323 of 324 printed I2 cells within tolerance; the mean of each replicate's I2 gives 17, the median 100.

assumptions.what: Each arm's mean and SD are drawn from their sampling distributions (mean ~ N(mu, SD^2/n), (n - 1) s^2/SD^2 ~ chi-squared with n - 1 df), which for normal data is the same in distribution as computing them from n values
assumptions.sensitivity: Drawing every patient instead (Table 3, all 36 settings) leaves 378 of 378 cells within tolerance (RMS z 0.94 against 0.97).

assumptions.what: A RoM study whose simulated mean is not positive (ln RoM undefined) is left out of its meta-analysis; the paper does not say
assumptions.sensitivity: Only Table 5 (SD 70) has any: 1917 of its 5,400,000 simulated studies. Leaving the whole replicate out instead leaves 378 of 378 cells of Table 5 within tolerance.

assumptions.what: SMD: the standard pooled SD sqrt(((n_e - 1) sd_e^2 + (n_c - 1) sd_c^2)/(N - 2)); the Appendix prints a stray '- 1' under the root. The small-sample factor 1 - 3/(4N - 9) and the variance N/(n_e n_c) + SMD^2/(2(N - 3.94)) as printed
assumptions.sensitivity: The pooled SD as printed, with '- 1', leaves 378 of 378 cells of Table 4 (SD 10, where it matters most) within tolerance. Without the small-sample factor, 352 of 378 cells of Table 3.

assumptions.what: Inverse-variance random effects with the DerSimonian-Laird tau2 and 95% CIs of the estimate +/- 1.96 SE (on ln RoM for RoM), as in the Methods and Appendix
assumptions.sensitivity: rommeta.pool equals R's metafor rma(method = 'DL') on 900 simulated meta-analyses to a relative 5e-14.

assumptions.what: Seeds: one NumPy 2.2.6 (PCG64) stream per scenario from [20080521, table, row, tau]; the paper's SAS 8.2 seeds are not given
assumptions.sensitivity: A second run with base seed 20080522 leaves 2,267 of 2,268 cells within tolerance; our two runs agree with each other within tolerance in 2,268 of 2,268 cells.

assumptions.what: Comparison tolerance, fixed before the comparison: half a printed unit plus 3 x sqrt(2) Monte Carlo standard errors of one 10,000-replicate estimate (bias: sd of the pooled estimates / 100; coverage and power: binomial; I2: delta method)
assumptions.sensitivity: Our run of a wrong design (another SD, the arms swapped, normal for skewed) leaves 59 to 111 of the 126 RoM cells of a table within tolerance (RMS z 2.4 or more); the right design leaves 125 or more. MD and SMD do not depend on the SD, so their columns cannot tell Tables 3, 4 and 5 apart: wrong designs reach 282 to 356 of all 378 cells.
